title: Why Is Smurfit WestRock Stock Falling?
paragraphs: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Smurfit WestRock (SW) shares fell 5.2% on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, while the S&P 500 rose 0.3%. The packaging maker posted the decline as it reported third-quarter results that fell short of analysts’ estimates for both earnings and revenue. So what held the quarter back, and what does management now expect for 2026?
What Held Back Smurfit WestRock’s Third Quarter?

News reports said higher costs and weak volumes held the quarter back, linking the miss to freight, energy and raw material expenses. Adjusted earnings came to $0.45 per share, short of the $0.60 consensus estimate, according to Zacks. Revenue reached $8.16 billion, below the $8.29 billion analysts expected.

Management called the cost inflation, mostly in energy and freight, unprecedented and greater than it had anticipated. It said it raised prices across most paper grades to counter those expenses, noting that the increases are passing through with a normal time lag. This means customers pay the new prices some time after the company’s own costs have already gone up.

Management also pointed to one-off events in the quarter, including heat waves in Europe and earthquakes in Colombia. A separate contamination issue in the U.S. agriculture sector hurt the company’s volumes in the United States and Mexico.

News reports noted the company lowered its 2026 outlook as well. Management now expects about $4.7 billion of adjusted EBITDA, its measure of profit before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, for 2026. It said energy costs alone will be about $700 million higher than a year earlier, running materially above earlier expectations. Management did point to demand, adding that corrugated volumes improved from the second quarter and practically all its paper grades remain sold out.
Did Smurfit WestRock Fall With Other Packaging Stocks?

Only partly. Four of the five companies on Smurfit WestRock’s peer list fell alongside it, but three of those peers posted smaller declines than Smurfit WestRock. O-I Glass fell 12.4%, while International Paper rose 3.3%. The materials sector, tracked by the XLB fund, rose 0.2% in the same session, indicating the drop was largely Smurfit WestRock’s own rather than its sector’s.

Declines of this magnitude are uncommon for the stock. Smurfit WestRock registered five sessions with a fall at least this large in the 365 days before this one. Its most recent bigger move in either direction was an 11.1% rise on July 24, 2026.

Over the past twelve months, the stock lost 3.1% including dividends, compared with a 14.0% return for the S&P 500. These losses are recent: the stock fell 14.4% in the three months to October 28, against a 4.4% gain for the index. The $40.33 close sits well below the 52-week closing high of $51.84 set on February 18, 2026, though it remains above the 52-week closing low of $32.79 from November 20, 2025.

Smurfit WestRock is expected to report its fourth-quarter 2026 results in February 2027. When those numbers arrive, full-year adjusted EBITDA, measured against the outlook management gave on the October 28 call, is the figure to watch.
